news.title: Women's football shouldn't be penalised by Uefa boycott - Nandy
news.lede: Lisa Nandy wants Gianni Infantino to resign but would not support an U20 Women's World Cup boycott. Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy says women's footballers should not be "penalised" by a potential boycott of next month's Under-20 Women's World Cup, as hosts Poland say they have received no notice of any withdrawals from European teams. European governing body Uefa and its 55 members have threatened to boycott Fifa competitions over its president Gianni Infantino's plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup. Poland are due to host the tournament from 5-27 September, but are not the only Uefa nation involved - with England, Italy, Spain, Portugal and France all due to take part.

news.title: Infantino’s opponents developing new framework for running world football
news.lede: Uefa, Concacaf and AFC working together on system. Fifa has ignored calls for an independent review. Gianni Infantino’s opponents are working together to produce a new framework for running world football to replace what they regard as a system of patronage that Fifa has adopted since he replaced Sepp Blatter as president 10 years ago. Repeated calls from Uefa, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation for an independent review of Fifa’s governance have been ignored by Infantino since this plan to sell off 21% of the World Cup was made public a fortnight ago, and the rebels are now understood to have taken matters into their own hands.

news.title: Donald Trump says it would be a ‘terrible mistake’ to replace Fifa’s Gianni Infantino
news.lede: US president backs ‘fantastic’ Infantino in Truth Social post. Infantino under pressure following doomed World Cup sell-off plan. US president Donald Trump has warned Fifa would be making a “terrible mistake” if they get rid of Gianni Infantino as the head of world football’s governing body. Infantino has come under pressure following his doomed plan to sell off stakes in the men’s World Cup to private investors.

news.title: Haissem Hassan: World Cup pedigree & La Liga experience - who is reported Celtic target?
news.lede: Haissem Hassan featured for Egypt against Argentina at this year's World Cup. Having burst on to the World Cup stage this summer, breakout star Haissem Hassan now appears bound for Celtic. The Egypt winger is reportedly set for a medical in Glasgow after Celtic agreed an initial £6m transfer fee, external, that could rise to £9m, with Real Oviedo. It would end a saga and take Celtic's haul of new recruits this summer to three as the hugely-important Champions League play-off with LASK looms large.

news.title: Morocco Leads Four African Teams to 2027 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: Rabat - Four continental contenders have officially booked their spots for the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil following intense quarter-final action at the Women's Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) in Morocco from late July through August 16. Morocco defeated South Africa 2-1 to seal a second consecutive tournament berth. Sakina Ouzraoui Diki and Hanane Ait El Haj found the net to send the Atlas Lionesses into the semi-finals on home soil. Speaking in a post-match press conference, head coach Jorge Vilda attributed the World Cup qualification to systemic institutional support.

news.title: Two wars and a World Cup lead to epic DDoS attacks on publishers
news.lede: Ukraine, Iran, and football inspire geopolitically motivated DDoS attacks, while 1 Tbps traffic jams up 519 percent. Ongoing wars in Ukraine and Iran and the FIFA World Cup all contributed to a DDoS walloping of media organizations throughout 2026 so far, according to Cloudflare’s latest data, which identified the sector as the most targeted this year. Attacks on media, production, and publishing accounted for 14.2 percent of all DDoS attacks launched since January 1. Over the first six months of the year, the sector saw nearly four times the number of attacks leveled at the second most-targeted sector, gambling and casinos, and six times more in Q2 alone.
